g.text: My Gamedev Journey
* Started in Unity
* "2D" heightmap terraingen
* Simple Material rastering w/colors
* Layers at arbitrary levels made into a color
* No trilinear shaders
* "3D" terraingen with Marching Cubes
* Took a long time, ~1mo of research
* Whitepapers, blogs/articles, videos, etc
* Naive implementation in ~2days
* Started learning Unity Jobs system
* Concurrent implementation in another ~2days
* Attempted Parallel implementation and got stuck
* Friend started tinkering with gamedev
* After some trial and error, they chose Godot
* Through helping them, I started seeing how easy Godot was to pick up
* After reluctancy, I started hammering out examples in GDScript
* I was now officially interested in Godot
* Saw another streamer working on their game, and the camera angle went all wonky
and an image flashed in my head from my childhood playing Descent.
This gave me an idea for a game.
* Started researching 6DOF flight mechanics, which instantly lead me to Quaternion Math.
* Spent a good bit learning the actual math, then I interrogated Grok LLM
about the intuition side.
* Got decent 6DOF flight mechanics knocked out, including per-axis damping mid-flight,
collisions, and all using Quaternions
* Started on alignment, got that knocked out quickly, but wanted a wobble at the end.
* This lead me into learning Hooke's Law, and Angular Damping on a Harmonic Oscillation.
* This took about 20 minutes to knock out, once I got the confidence to try.
* Didn't like how the alignment was working, and broke it all.
* Decided to build a Debug Draw for runtime.
* This broke my understanding of Basis/GlobalBasis, and transforming coordinates spaces.
* Spent a solid day with Grok learning these concepts.
* Knocked out the DebugDraw in a few hours.
* Still learning about some vector/Euclidean math regarding axis alignment and projections.
